newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM says business as usual after raid on PS.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM says business as usual after raid on PS.

text.p: Police raided the headquarters of Belgium's scandal-hit Francophone Socialist Party (PS) on Tuesday but Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's office said his centre-left government was carrying on business as normal.

The Belgian franc came under pressure after the raid on the accounts section of the PS as part of enquiries into a new bribery scandal as the four-party coalition government fought to ignore opposition calls to resign and keep a sense of calm.
"The government is not troubled by this investigation. It does not concern any government member, it is an internal problem of the PS," Dehaene's spokeswoman told Reuters.
Social Affairs Minister Magda de Galan said her party had "received the message loud and clear" from Dehaene that the PS should clean up its act and make clear who was to blame.
"We know what we have to do," she said, without elaborating.
The PS is the second most powerful partner in Belgium's four-party coalition government with the Flemish Socialists and the French- and Flemish-speaking Christian Democratic parties.

The latest scandal erupted when Merry Hermanus and Francois Pirot, two former top PS officials, were charged on Monday with corruption as part of a probe into allegations that the party received kickbacks from French aviation firm Dassault in 1989.
Dassault has denied any wrongdoing.
Hermanus says that Guy Spitaels, then PS president and currently president of the Walloon Regional Parliament, knew of the contribution, according to his lawyer.

Spitaels, forced to resign in 1994 during investigations into bribes allegedly paid to the PS in the late 1980s by Italian helicopter firm Agusta in exchange for a lucrative army contract, denies all knowledge of the Dassault money.
Spitaels was re-elected in 1995.

But the national mood has become less forgiving of corruption since the rescue last August of two sexually abused young girls and the subsequent discovery of four dead children on properties linked to convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux.

The Agusta investigations also brought down NATO Secretary General and Flemish Socialist Party member Willy Claes 18 months ago. Claes, who was Economy Minister at the end of the 1980s, also maintains his innocence and Agusta says it did nothing wrong.
Claude Eerdekens, head of the PS parliamentary party, told RTBF television there was a possibility the chamber might be forced to lift Spitaels's ministerial immunity from prosecution.
Philippe Busquin, current president of the PS and also implicated in the Dassault affair by Hermanus, also denied any knowledge of the latest allegations.
The scandal is the latest in a string of set-backs for the government and the PS in particular.

In December, after weeks of turmoil, the government used its parliamentary muscle to throw out a string of allegations that Deputy Prime Minister and PS member Elio Di Rupo had sex with boys under the legal age of consent of 16 years.
Di Rupo had always rejected the allegations but the parliamentary move nevetherless prompted cries of cover-up.
National elections are not due until 1999, but if the PS does succumb to the pressure and quit the coalition the government will fall.

However Dehaene, with his eyes firmly set on Belgium joining the European Union's single currency at the start of 1999, is anxious to avoid either changing partners in mid-stream or calling early elections.
